text:
tessa: Quick post from the onboarding session: a bunch of new users hit 429s when using the Node quickstart to page through historical embeddings.
mohit: thanks — reproduced. The demo aggressively fires parallel page requests and the client-side retry logic retries immediately without jitter. That amplifies quota bursts.
carla: what's the demo doing exactly?
tessa: gist is `await Promise.all(pageCursors.map(c => client.embeddings.page({ cursor: c })))` then inside page handler it calls `client.embeddings.create` for each item with no concurrency guard.
mohit: double problem: unbounded page concurrency + per-item parallel creates = exponential request fanout. Also the auth refresh path races: when token refresh occurs mid-stream, many requests get 401 and then back-to-back retries.
carla: SDK parity note: Python has a public RateLimiter and a stream-aware controller; JS keeps those primitives inside the runtime. That makes it hard for sample apps to coordinate.
tessa: short term fix I'm pushing: (A) change demo to async iterator + semaphore, example: `const limit = pLimit(4); for await (const page of client.embeddings.paginate(q)) { await limit(() => processPage(page)); }` (B) wire AbortController to stop inflight work on errors.
mohit: good. For retries let's adopt bounded exponential backoff with jitter client-side: `delay = Math.min(1500, 100 * 2**attempt) * (0.6 + Math.random()*0.8)`. Keeps retries spaced and prevents immediate thundering.
carla: long-term: export a tiny `createRateController({permitsPerSecond, burst})` and a `paginate(..., {concurrency})` option from the JS SDK so samples don't need external libs. Also add `auth.singleflight()` to serialize token refreshes.
tessa: also adding these lightweight headers to requests so support can correlate client behavior: `x-client-stream-id`, `x-client-concurrency`. Low-risk and very helpful.
mohit: agree. Another subtle bug: the demo retries on 401/429 in a way that doesn't respect AbortController signals, so cancellation doesn't stop retry loops. We should ensure retry loop checks `signal.aborted` before each attempt.
carla: telemetry idea: add a dev-only meter exposed via `client.__diagnostics()` in non-prod builds that reports current token-bucket tokens, queue length, and avg page latency. Useful for quickstarts and for customers tuning concurrency.
tessa: support spin-up: will add a KB blurb "Quickstart: 429s while paging" with recommended immediate steps: reduce concurrency, use p-limit fallback, enable jittered backoff, use AbortController, and link the demo PR.
kb-bot: KB created: https://kb.redwood-inference.dev/quickstart-pagination-429s (internal).
mohit: I'll open an SDK PR to export the minimal rate controller and the `paginate(..., { concurrency: 2 })` opt. Carla: can you take the auth.singleflight PR?
carla: on it. I'll also add tests that simulate token rotations and assert no thundering herd.
tessa: deploy preview incoming: https://deployments.redwood-inference.dev/pr/990 (demo uses p-limit + AbortController and includes KB link).
mohit: plan: demo patch + KB -> ship today. SDK primitives + auth.singleflight + diagnostics -> next sprint.
carla: add support checklist item: "If a customer reports 429s during pagination: 1) ask for x-client-concurrency header, 2) recommend quickstart patch, 3) escalate if it's affecting production quota."
tessa: thanks team. this should make onboarding less noisy and reduce tickets. :sparkles:
